events.title: Darius I Organizes the Persian Empire
events.description: Darius I divides the empire into 20 satrapies with efficient administration, a postal system, and the "Royal Road" from Sardis to Susa – 2,700 km long.

events.title: Persepolis Is Built
events.description: Darius I begins construction of Persepolis, the ceremonial capital of the Persian Empire, with magnificent palaces and reliefs.

events.title: The Battle of Marathon
events.description: Athens defeats a Persian invasion force at Marathon. The messenger Pheidippides runs to Athens with news of victory – the origin of the marathon race.

events.title: Thermopylae and Salamis
events.description: King Xerxes of Persia invades Greece with a massive army. 300 Spartans hold the pass at Thermopylae. Athens crushes the Persian fleet at Salamis.

events.title: The Golden Age of Athens
events.description: Under Pericles' leadership, Athens experiences an unprecedented flourishing of democracy, art, architecture, drama, and philosophy.

events.title: Parthenon Built
events.description: The temple to Athena is built on the Acropolis in Athens, designed by Iktinos and Kallikrates. It is still regarded as a masterpiece of architecture.

events.title: Herodotus – The Father of History
events.description: Herodotus writes his "Histories" about the Greco-Persian Wars and cultures around the Mediterranean. He is considered the first historian.

events.title: Peloponnesian War
events.description: Athens and Sparta fight a devastating war that lasts for 27 years. Sparta wins, but all of Greece is weakened.

events.title: Socrates
events.description: Socrates teaches in Athens through his dialectical method. He is sentenced to death in 399 BC for "corrupting the youth" and "introducing new gods".

events.title: Plato and the Academy
events.description: Plato, a student of Socrates, founds the Academy in Athens—the first institution of higher learning in the Western world. He writes dialogues on justice, beauty, and truth.

events.title: Hippocrates – the father of medicine
events.description: Hippocrates on Kos lays the foundation for medicine as a science, based on observation rather than superstition. The Hippocratic Oath is still used today.

events.title: The Elephantine Papyri
events.description: Jewish mercenaries in Elephantine in Egypt left behind papyrus documents showing that there was a Jewish temple there, with correspondence to Jerusalem.
